citation: 'Residence of Mr. Marshall Field, 1905 Prairie Avenue.' Halftone plate, photographer uncredited. Rand, McNally & Co.'s Pictorial Chicago (Chicago: Rand, McNally & Co., 1893).
author: Rand, McNally & Co. (publisher); photographer uncredited
repository: Internet Archive, randmcnallycospi00rand_0 (the 1893 edition of Pictorial Chicago, the book the Ream plate (rand_mcnally_pictorial_chicago_1893_ream) comes from). Prairie library image a19-pictorial-1893-field; the image store's display copy (kevinrhaas/chicago-images, prairie-1904/files/a19-pictorial-1893-field.jpg).
locator: The plate captioned 'Residence of Mr. Marshall Field, 1905 Prairie Avenue': the house from across Prairie Avenue to the south-west, the street front with the door numbered 1905, the canted south-west corner, the south flank's front part with the curved conservatory, the bracketed cornice over a frieze, the slated mansard with its dormers and iron cresting, the raised stone basement and the scroll-pattern iron fence; bare street trees before the corner.
rights_note: Published in the United States in 1893, so in the public domain. The reference copy committed for the image gate (data/sources/assets/field_1905_pictures_t3260/pictorial_1893_field_plate.jpg) is the store's display copy of the page cropped to the plate's border and not otherwise altered; nothing is derived from it as an asset.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-30 (T-3260) from the image store's display copy of the page, 1600 x 1233 px (sha256 bdee57d5d8c63e85c949b99b9cbe52ea983931b214d23de69aa27aa1dfe18cee). The plate's page number in the Archive's scan was not read: the store's copy carries the caption, not the leaf.
note: The earliest dated photograph of the Field house in the Prairie library, and the clearest: the camera is a view camera with a raised front (the verticals stand parallel), from the avenue's far side about 30 m off the corner. Its camera is solved in data/reference_views/marshall_field_house_1905_prairie/pictorial_1893_plate.json.
what_it_supplies: the street front's composition by 1893: a blank brick end at the north, a window column, the door bay (the door numbered 1905), a narrow window column and a wide one, then the blank canted corner

two storeys of brick, dark against its light stone dressings, over a raised light stone basement, a stone belt at the chamber floor, a bracketed cornice over a frieze of roundels, a slated mansard with dormers and an iron cresting
the south flank's curved one-storey conservatory with a balcony on its roof
what_it_does_not_supply: colour: the plate is a monochrome halftone
the north flank, the rear and the rear ranges
the house in 1904: it shows it by 1893
